title: Biology, diagnosis and treatment of Malassezia dermatitis in dogs and cats: Clinical Consensus Guidelines of the World Association for Veterinary Dermatology
citation: Bond R, et al. Vet Dermatol. 2020;31(1):28-74. doi:10.1111/vde.12809. PMID:31957204
evidence_type: WAVD clinical consensus guideline with literature review
key_points: Topical therapy is important for Malassezia dermatitis; 2% miconazole plus 2% chlorhexidine shampoo twice weekly has strong supportive evidence.
Itraconazole and ketoconazole have evidence for systemic treatment in dogs when topical therapy is insufficient or impractical.
Clinical improvement should be interpreted together with cytology and management of underlying disease.

topics: 皮膚エリテマトーデス
title: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus in dogs: a comprehensive review
citation: Olivry T, Linder KE, Banovic F. BMC Vet Res. 2018;14:132. doi:10.1186/s12917-018-1446-8. PMID:29669547
evidence_type: Comprehensive disease review of published canine CLE cases/series
key_points: Canine CLE comprises multiple subtypes with different treatment responses; subtype and extent matter when selecting therapy.
Published regimens include topical tacrolimus for localized disease and systemic glucocorticoids/ciclosporin for selected generalized or severe forms.
Evidence is largely case series and small clinical studies rather than large randomized trials.

title: Use of mycophenolate mofetil to treat immune-mediated skin disease in 14 dogs - a retrospective evaluation
citation: Ackermann AL, May ER, Frank LA. Vet Dermatol. 2017;28(2):195-e44. doi:10.1111/vde.12400. PMID:27943548
key_points: Fourteen dogs received MMF with glucocorticoids; mean MMF dose was 14.7 mg/kg twice daily.
Ten of 14 dogs had a positive response, including eight complete remissions.
This is retrospective evidence and does not establish a universally optimal dose.

title: Canine sterile nodular panniculitis: a retrospective study of 14 cases
key_points: Sterile nodular panniculitis may be a marker of concurrent systemic disease; infectious causes and concurrent disease should be investigated.
Dogs treated with immunosuppressive corticosteroids generally responded.
Prognosis and treatment decisions depend on the underlying disease process.

topics: 皮膚エリテマトーデス
title: Successful treatment of a novel generalized variant of canine discoid lupus erythematosus with oral hydroxychloroquine
citation: Oberkirchner U, Linder KE, Olivry T. Vet Dermatol. 2012;23(1):65-70,e15-16. doi:10.1111/j.1365-3164.2011.00994.x. PMID:21718370
key_points: A dog with generalized discoid lupus achieved long-term control with hydroxychloroquine 5 mg/kg orally once daily, with topical therapy during flares.
Relapse occurred when dosing frequency was reduced, underscoring that this is individual case evidence rather than a standard regimen.

title: Use of tetracycline and niacinamide for treatment of autoimmune skin disease in 31 dogs
citation: White SD, Rosychuk RA, Reinke SI, Paradis M. J Am Vet Med Assoc. 1992;200(10):1497-1500. PMID:1535346
key_points: The combination was evaluated in 31 dogs with autoimmune skin disease; 70% of dogs with discoid lupus had good or excellent responses.
Modern antimicrobial stewardship should be considered before using an antibiotic primarily for immunomodulation.
